title: The pull-push approximation diagram and its counit cocone
statement: Let I be a small category, D:I→Sch a diagram, s a cone with vertex X and projections p_i:X→D_i, and F an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use the inverse/direct image adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image; def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Define A:I^op→Ab(X_et) by A_i=p_i^*p_i*F. For f:j→i, its map A_i→A_j is the adjunction transpose of p_i*F→p_ji*p_j*F→p_ji*p_j*p_j^*p_j*F→p_i*p_j^*p_j*F, using direct-image composition and the unit at p_j*F. These maps satisfy identity and composition. The counits A_i→F form a cocone, and q:colim A→F denotes its comparison map.

source.place: Proof step 1: The pull-push approximation diagram and its counit cocone

proof.text: Define the transition by the displayed adjunction transpose. Its transpose formula is the hom-equivalence inverse identity.

Transpose equality with the counit and use the triangle identity to obtain compatibility of the counits. The right-unit coherence of direct-image composition gives identity maps. For composition, transpose both composites, use naturality of the composition isomorphism, then its associativity coherence; the two transposes agree.
Use these equations as the functor and cocone laws. Define the comparison by colimit.desc; no choice from an existence theorem or unfinished data construction is used.
